t: #3852 Smallest Pair With Different Frequencies — Frequency Table Scan
o: Among distinct values x < y with freq(x) != freq(y), return the lexicographically smallest [x, y]. With values bounded by 100, collect frequencies, sort distinct values, and for each x in ascending order scan larger y until a frequency mismatch appears — the first hit is the answer. Examples: [1,1,2,2,3,4] -> [1,3]; [1,5] and [7] -> [-1,-1].
k: Sorting distinct values ascending guarantees the first valid (x, y) found is lexicographically smallest.
Values <= 100 means at most 100 distinct values, so an O(V^2) scan is instant.

a.n: Approach 1: Frequency map + sorted double loop
a.i: Count frequencies with a hash map, iterate distinct values in increasing order, and return the first pair (x, y), x < y, whose frequencies differ.
s: Extract and sort the distinct values.
For each i < j pair in order, return [vals[i], vals[j]] on the first frequency mismatch.
a.t: O(n + V^2) with V <= 100 distinct values — effectively O(n).

w: Tiny constraints make this a correctness exercise more than an efficiency one. Pitfalls: forgetting pairs require distinct values (x < y excludes x == y), and returning pairs with equal frequencies. A follow-up could raise the value range, where you would instead bucket values by frequency and, for each x, look up the nearest larger value with a different frequency using sorted structures.
